title: Filter the list down
brief:
Eight products are on screen. Two of them are dresses. Write one locator that matches **exactly the two dress cards** - not the eight cards, not the two `

` tags holding their names, the two `.productinfo` cards themselves. The tool for this is `.filter(has_text="...")`: start from all the cards, then keep only the ones containing some text.

checks.name: to_have_count
checks.label: It matches exactly the two dress cards

checks.name: filter
checks.label: You narrowed the list with .filter()
checks.feedback: You landed on two elements, but not by filtering. `.nth(2)` and friends depend on the catalogue never being reordered; `.filter(has_text="Dress")` says what you actually mean and keeps working when a ninth product arrives.

hints.label: Nudge
hints.text: Start from the whole set - locator(".productinfo") gives you all eight - then narrow it.

hints.label: Strategy
hints.text: Both dresses have "Dress" in their names: Sleeveless Dress and Stylish Dress. has_text matches a substring and ignores case.

reveal:
`.filter()` is the one narrowing tool that describes **meaning** rather than **position**, which is why it survives changes that break `.nth()`.

Watch the outlines in the shop panel: the whole card is highlighted, not just the name. Filtering keeps the elements you started from - it does not descend into them.
